post.title: How a Tree Eats Air
post.hook: Nearly all of a tree's weight came from thin air, not the soil.
post.summary: A single-page interactive simulation of tree photosynthesis, carbon allocation and growth, with a live iteration trace of every equation. It lets you run a tree from seed through 1000 years.
post.writeup:
## What it is
A single HTML page, "How a Tree Eats Air", that simulates a tree's carbon and oxygen budget. You pick a tree type (deciduous, evergreen, redwood), set sunlight, CO₂, soil water and climate, then watch a seedling turn gas into structure.

## Why
To make a counter-intuitive fact visible: a tree's mass mostly comes from air. The page states that 95% of the tree's dry mass was pulled out of thin air and water, not the soil.

## How it works
Photosynthesis uses a non-rectangular hyperbola light response, scaled by a CO₂ Michaelis term and a RuBisCO temperature bell peaking at 27°C. Respiration is maintenance plus growth respiration (~28% of what's built). Net production is split across leaves 25%, stem 30%, branches 20% and roots 25%, with the leaf share tapering as the canopy fills, which gives an S-shaped growth curve. Stoichiometry is exact: 1 O₂ released per CO₂ fixed.

The UI has three parts: the leaf as a photosynthesis engine, the tree as a carbon ledger, and growth over time with seasons. A "Math mode" iteration trace steps one 0.02-day sub-step (~29 min) at a time and shows every equation live. You can fast forward +1, +10, +100 or +1000 years.

## Findings
Defaults start at Sunlight 100%, CO₂ 420 ppm and Soil water 75%. The page also retells Van Helmont's 1640s willow: it gained ~74 kg while the soil lost only ~57 g.

## Open questions
The constants are tuned for legibility over a browsable timescale, not for a specific species, so outputs are order-of-magnitude. Calibrating against real species data would be the next step.
